text:
postmortem-bot: New postmortem created: INCIDENT-2026-14 (hosted API small-batch tail latency). link: https://pm.redwood/INCIDENT-2026-14
maya: TL;DR: small bursts of short sequences caused KV-cache thrashing -> fallback to cold KV read -> burst tail latency spikes. Postmortem outlines root cause and a few immediate mitigations.
ryan: thanks — we need concrete follow-ups: remediation ownership, test additions, and a timeline. who wants to take the regression pieces?
sasha: I can take the prompt/regression set. we should capture the exact request patterns that triggered it (short seq, many concurrent small batches).
annie: I'll own the load-test harness changes (parallelism and warm-cache scenarios). plan: add a new scenario in load-tests called `small-batch-kv-warmup`.
samir: i'll coordinate the chaos drill. suggestion: simulate 1) cache invalidation, 2) short bursts from many clients, 3) partial GPU node reboots.
maya: action items I want tracked in the postmortem follow-ups section. propose we create small tickets and latch them to the incident so SRE/product can track.
ryan: owning end-to-end: I'll make the tracker board and link the 4 tickets.
maya: quick draft of tickets (short):
- T1: eval/regression: reproduce burst with saved prompts and add to nightly. owner: sasha. due: 2026-04-05.
- T2: load-test: add warm-cache and cold-cache variants + scaling params. owner: annie. due: 2026-04-07.
- T3: runtime fix: guard to avoid synchronous cold KV fallback under heavy concurrency. owner: infra-team (samir liaise). due: 2026-04-12.
- T4: chaos drill + runbook update for KV swaps. owner: samir. due: 2026-04-20.
sasha: agreed on T1. I already started a branch: `github.com/redwood-inference/evals/compare/incident-2026-14`. will add a prompt set file `incident-2026-14/prompts.json` with 120 short prompts mirroring production traces.
annie: for T2, proposed load command:
```
./scripts/run_load --suite small-batch-kv-warmup --clients 200 --qps 400 --cache-warmups 10
```
we'll also add warmup sequences to avoid hitting cold-path during steady state tests.
ryan: can we add the regression as part of the presubmit gating for runtime PRs? we need to ensure new runtime changes don't regress.
maya: yes, add regression to `nightly-evals` and a lightweight presubmit check for PRs touching KV/cache paths. short runtimes ok — maybe run a 5-min smoke that uses the small-batch prompt set.
sasha: note: we should version the prompt set and keep it minimal to avoid flakiness. I'll include expected latency buckets so tests assert tail < 200ms for warm-cache scenario.
samir: regarding recurring patterns: I've looked at metrics — similar spikes happened 3x in last 6 months but with different triggers. seems like short-burst workload is an emergent pattern. we should add a periodic (monthly) regression that simulates burstiness.
annie: putting that in the runbook: add instruction to run `small-batch-kv-warmup` as part of monthly chaos drill and record traces to S3 with folder `incidents/2026-14/`.
ryan: I'll create the tracker board now and post links to the tickets.
ryan: created board: https://board.redwood/boards/INCIDENT-2026-14
ryan: tickets created:
- RNW-2123 T1 eval/regression (assignee: sasha) https://pm.redwood/Tickets/2123
- RNW-2124 T2 load-test (assignee: annie) https://pm.redwood/Tickets/2124
- RNW-2125 T3 runtime-guard (assignee: infra-team) https://pm.redwood/Tickets/2125
- RNW-2126 T4 chaos drill (assignee: samir) https://pm.redwood/Tickets/2126
maya: smallest follow-up: add an eval alert when nightly regression fails. link alert to #incidents and create pager policy for dedicated customers only.
sasha: quick note on implementation: prompt set will be JSON lines with metadata: client_id, seq_len, tokens_count. will include replay harness support: `python replay.py --prompts incident-2026-14/prompts.json`.
annie: for load infra I'll add a GCP job and a dedicated runner. will open a PR to `eng-load` repo and ping @ryan for presubmit gating.
samir: chaos drill timeline proposal: run on 2026-04-22 09:00 PT (out of peak for EMEA). 2-hour window, dry-run a week before. any objections?
maya: looks good to me. +1 for dry-run.
ryan: timeline from now:
- by 2026-03-26: board + tickets (done)
- by 2026-04-05: regression added to nightly (sasha)
- by 2026-04-07: load-test infra & job (annie)
- by 2026-04-12: runtime guard PR (infra)
- by 2026-04-20: chaos dry-run complete
- by 2026-04-22: chaos drill run
please update ticket comments when done.
annie: quick question: who will own the presubmit alert integration? I'd like to avoid noisy pages during tests.
ryan: I'll coordinate with oncall to make the presubmit alert non-pager for the first week, escalate if flapping.
maya: small follow-up: add evaluation docs to the postmortem doc linking to the prompt set, load config, and reproducible commands. I'll add that section now.
sasha: PR opened for prompts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/187 — details in PR description includes expected-latency buckets and reproducible seed.
annie: PR for load infra: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-load/pull/43
samir: runtime guard draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/901 (WIP)
postmortem-bot: Postmortem updated: INCIDENT-2026-14 follow-ups added (4 tickets).
maya: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene next week for a short sync. please add any blockers to the ticket comments. :thumbsup: 
ryan: ack. I'll add a quick 15m sync on Mon.
sasha: ack, will finish prompt set tests tonight.
annie: will start infra job tomorrow morning.
samir: prepping chaos checklist, will post in #incidents and #eng-sre.
maya: closing thread for now — updates go on the board and tickets.
